cards.explanation: The answer is True. The voices say, "Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you." (Song of Solomon 6:13) The Shulammite is the young woman of this love poem. That's a whole lot of calling just to get a good look at her, friends.

The answer is False. The description starts at her feet: "How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince!" (Song of Solomon 7:1) Then it works up to her neck, her eyes and her head. It's a trip from the ground to the crown, friends.

The answer is the king. The poem says, "the king is captured in your tresses." (Song of Solomon 7:5) Her hair is like purple threads, and the king is caught right in it. I've been stuck in a junk drawer, friends, but never in anything that pretty.

The answer is False. The speaker says, "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit." (Song of Solomon 7:8) Nobody here is staying back, friends. This speaker has a plan, and the plan is UP.

The answer is that she is his and his desire is for her. She says, "I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me." (Song of Solomon 7:10) It's short, and she says it plainly. After all that poetry about her, friends, she speaks for herself in one line.

The answer is True. She says, "Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers." (Song of Solomon 7:11) She's the one doing the inviting here, friends. She's the one who asks him to come along.

The answer is whether the vine has budded and the blossom has opened. She wants to see "…if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom…" (Song of Solomon 7:12) She names the vine, the blossom and the pomegranates. It's buds and blooms she's watching for, friends.

The answer is every delicacy she has treasured up for him. She says, "…at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved." (Song of Solomon 7:13) She saved up new ones and old ones. That's more planning than I've done for any batch, friends.

The answer is so she could kiss him outdoors and not be despised. She says, "If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me." (Song of Solomon 8:1) She wants that kind of ease with him in public, friends. The text gives that as her wish.

The answer is mother. She says, "I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me." (Song of Solomon 8:2) Then she adds spiced wine and the nectar of her pomegranates. Her mother's house is where she wants to bring him, friends.
